title: Heisenberg Uncertainty from Complex Cauchy-Schwarz
description: Derives the Heisenberg uncertainty principle σ_x·σ_p ≥ ℏ/2 from the complex Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Pure algebraic derivation in abstract inner product spaces.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: Uses Mathlib's Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (inner_mul_le_norm_mul_sq) as the foundation of the derivation chain.

overview.problemStatement: Can the Heisenberg uncertainty principle be derived from the complex Cauchy-Schwarz inequality?
keyInsights: Pure algebraic derivation — works in any complex inner product space

conclusion.summary: YES. The uncertainty principle is a direct consequence of Cauchy-Schwarz applied to centered observables, plus the imaginary part bound.
conclusion.implications: YES. The uncertainty principle is a direct consequence of Cauchy-Schwarz applied to centered observables, plus the imaginary part bound.
